ef9748393af233c9: The three combat styles a squad can take
992e3fec1e41dec5: Formation{a=00} lets a squad of two or three units change how it lines up, changing its combat ability with it.{/a}
fb8383fadb8e203f: There are three, and you can switch freely until the squad ends its action.
0875f8b1c4ef8ce4: The enemy uses them too, so learn what each does and which beats which.
e87ddf4431cb37e5: The basic form, and the only one with Tri Charge
c19ed78e43779d1f: The leader takes point, members in single file behind. Squads always deploy this way. Its great advantage is that it alone can use {a=0e}Tri Charge{/a}, a pseudo-combination attack.
3d4764bc9551d2d0: Members join no attack but Tri Charge; in exchange the leader shields them, so they gain a defence bonus. Only Support Def protects the leader, so pick a tough unit that will not be shot down.
3d970710083abd53: ・Attacks on members have -20% final hit rate.
f0363669d149486e: ・Tri Charge needs a full squad of three.

de90ae36e29071ba: Members close up in front. The squad can hit one unit of the enemy squad with a Squad Atk, then have the leader attack it too. If any unit in the squad has a barrier, {a=0e}Squad Barrier{/a} applies it to the whole squad.

6a3b36be79c8e49a: ・Leader gets +20% final hit rate on a Squad Atk.
13a9d13d5c4f6681: Leader and members spread out wide, making members resistant to All Atk and cutting the damage they take sharply.
95367ef1897f8c23: On a Squad Atk each of your units picks a different target in the enemy squad.
19010bf678b798f9: Give the squad a leader whose Leader effect raises Squad Atk damage and you deal more still.
412a2db8a3377e7c: ・A Squad Atk can hit several enemies. (member damage is 80% of normal)
4fc48706e6a06d0a: The formations beat one another in a cycle
14aea08ed8bb498d: Each formation is strong against one and weak to another, a triangle like rock-paper-scissors, so your choice can swing a fight.
1894f4ffac1c566b: Attacking:{a=03} Tri Charge negates their Squad Barrier.{/a}
3a8025d046378139: Defending:{a=03} Support Def blocks a Squad Atk's massed fire.{/a}
a2dab2079ebf2d1e: Attacking:{a=07} Members block 50% of Tri Charge damage.{/a}
dddfb49742d113ae: Defending:{a=07} The members behind are targeted too.{/a}
a58769b207675991: Attacking:{a=07} Even massed Squad Atk fire is stopped by Support Def.{/a}
8cdee0e6849a770d: Defending:{a=07} Tri Charge negates your Squad Barrier.{/a}

0dcef30b530376f5: Attacking:{a=03} You can reach the members behind as well.{/a}
716fb39c168e4ca8: Defending:{a=03} Members cut Tri Charge damage by 50%.{/a}
89a05da9e889c110: Attacking:{a=07} You try to pick them off, but Squad Barrier holds.{/a}

4dc2666f05c94026: How far a squad can move
62a6a82895045f2f: Every unit has a Move, the distance it can travel, and a Move Type, the terrain it is suited to. Together they are written {a=0e}'Move / Move Type'{/a}. The two decide a squad's {a=0e}'Squad Move / Squad Move Type'{/a}.
b7b2372031f3b0e4: Squad Move is the average of its units' Move, rounded down. A squad normally travels that far, but rougher ground tends to cost more; what a tile costs to cross is its {a=0e}Move Cost{/a}.
bd512b9b92ddcd04: Accel{a=00} gives Squad Move +2 and {/a}Swift{a=00} +4, so a unit with one of them in each squad lets you advance quickly.{/a}
e58ec363f4bf60c8: Some Parts raise a unit's Move. The two below are the common ones, but others do the same.
0b5116357fb2690d: Squad Move rises most efficiently when the units' Move totals {a=0e}a multiple of the squad size (2 for two units, 3 for three){/a}.
2cd3d7e3f54269cb: Move Type depends on the combination
5e02463bb4e008ce: Squad Move Type{a=00} is decided by whether the squad's units have a Move Type for {/a}Air, Land and Water{a=00}. It sets how much Move each terrain costs to cross.{/a}
d3dd34292ef18aeb: If every unit in the squad has that terrain's Move Type, the Squad Move Type shows white, meaning it can move there. When {a=0e}Air{/a} is white the squad can change its terrain to air.
d8761975070158d9: If any unit lacks it, the type shows grey, meaning movement is hard. If no unit can move there it is blank, and the squad can barely advance, or cannot enter at all.
d467a2b597ddeb85: Parts can change a unit's Move Type. Build squads from units of the same type where you can, and keep the Squad Move Type white.
7232f4c9cafaddf9: ※Battleships have their own Move Types, air-only or land-only, so the Parts above cannot give them another.

9de95a6b7eabacb8: Some Spirits raise damage directly, others help you land it well. Used when needed, they lift your damage enormously.
b105f1237693c9cc: SP is limited, so judge where to spend it - against tough enemies, for instance.

aa42f9a352e6ee22: And {a=0e}Skill Learning{/a} teaches skills that raise damage in particular situations.
d181bf282b2f67e0: Joining a Support Atk makes that attack a sure critical.
700e6e39260605e9: Joining a Squad Atk deals 1.2 times normal Squad Atk damage.
0f907b9e66104aca: On an All Atk, gives back 15% of the damage lost to the enemy squad's size.

4dcdbb4421c09248: Cuts the armor of an enemy it hits by 200 for one turn.

a399032301151a8c: The attack type you choose can deal more than a normal attack. These are the main ones.
b7cec423b6d4f769: The members fire PLA weapons, then, or at the same time, the leader attacks. It adds hits as well as damage, so the enemy's Will tends to rise.

a28d89e952a253c2: And when the attacking enemy unit's {a=0e}Size{/a} is larger than yours, evade rate gains a bonus. There are five sizes, {a=0e}3L, 2L, L, M and S{/a}, and the wider the gap the larger the adjustment.
1bed830ae6f2c07e: Use the terrain of the battle map
1d4a3c5d1cc1c60b: Evade rate also shifts with the {a=0e}unit's Terrain rating{/a}, drawn from the unit's and the pilot's. There are {a=0e}five grades, S, A, B, C and D (-){/a}, and S gives the best evade rate.
b483beb0b6853043: Distance makes an attack harder to land
e46cce765e8b2bf2: {a=03}The further you stand from your target, the higher the evade rate{/a}. Move squads you cannot afford to lose away from the enemy, and outside weapon range if you can.
0b8e4e7440b7d1b9: Choose to evade when it matters
3312dfac6f654787: In Tri Formation the members' evade rate gains +20%.
035c1482072dc9da: And if you will give up your counter, choosing {a=0e}Evade{/a}, which halves the final hit rate, is the surest way to raise it.
2b6f2a87b9d051cd: A value that weighs heavily on combat damage
04265e7efa38edc8: Will{a=00} is the pilot stat affecting the damage you deal and the damage you take. It also gates weapon use and the triggering of {/a}skills{a=00} and {/a}abilities{a=00}, which makes raising it in battle the first thing to attend to.{/a}
7f13057dad19446c: This section covers several ways to raise a pilot's Will.
a56f58be7f272744: A pilot's Will rises and falls with each round of combat. Which actions move it depends on the pilot's {a=0e}Nature{/a}.
d9e27fd3fe3dd9b5: A bold pilot grows angry and gains Will when an ally is shot down. A timid one shrinks instead, and loses it.
df012e15c1da9a69: Will rises on a kill too, but the harder the {a=0e}difficulty{/a} (HARD, then NORMAL, then EASY), the less it rises.
59bd75896b56d276: The commands below lower Will as well. Even then it never falls below 100.
c866fc60bfe3dd0a: Being {a=0e}loaded{/a} onto or {a=0e}recovered{/a} by a battleship
4e64bb3d413fb4a7: Spirits raise it all at once
78a8e56950417ff8: Spirits{a=00} that raise Will let you use powerful weapons and skills that need Will from the moment a battle map opens. These are the main ones.{/a}
480382235f83a0ce: Raises every pilot in the squad's Will by 5 (yourself included).
c55e997adaace4fe: Many of a pilot's {a=0e}skills{/a} bear on Will. Here is the list - pick the ones that suit the unit and teach them.
e21960a4f8b4c57f: Sortie with Will +5. Ideal for the pilot of a unit with many weapons that need Will.
21ca84439ca10d63: Will +3 at the start of every player phase, from the turn after sortie. It suits a slow, careful style of play.
4ce983952b39efdc: Evading an attack grants an extra Will +1 on top of the normal change. Good for a pilot who dodges well.
8a9603964b3c073e: Landing a hit grants an extra Will +1. Recommended for a pilot who holds the front and counters.
580e8c41b240fca2: Taking damage grants an extra Will +2. It suits a super robot pilot who stands and takes attacks rather than dodging.
b29a28f4e6f576ee: When your squad shoots a unit down, or wipes out an enemy squad, an extra Will +1. Useful on any pilot.
64c239f36ab1153f: The Will cap of 150 becomes 170. More effective still on a unit with high Attack.
9ddc4f42bdcab5c8: A pilot with 50 kills or more earns 1.2 times the Funds from a kill and sorties with Will +5.
a82f7af2ec440ce6: The three pilots with the most kills sortie with Will +5. It stacks with {a=03}Ace Pilot{/a}, so the two together can give Will +10.
244b5b4c14bab736: You need a Repair or Resupply Module
79eb6ee21c82f3f8: Attacking blindly will not win a battle. At times you must repair damaged units and resupply those low on EN or ammo.
75ebdc6fb2ab3bed: The sections that follow cover the two commands that back your allies up, and the other ways to recover. Use them all to carry your force to victory.
9410123e0360aeeb: A command open to a unit with the {a=0e}Repair Module{/a} ability. It repairs every adjacent unit and every unit of the same squad. The higher the repairing pilot's level, the more HP it restores.
24cd77f833476a26: When that pilot has the {a=0e}Repair Skill{/a}, the HP restored is 1.5 times normal.
7c0aac243d9c64b2: A squad holding a unit with a Repair Module also gains the {a=0e}HP Regen{/a} squad bonus: right at the start of the player phase, {a=03}each unit recovers 10% of its HP for every Repair Module unit in the squad{/a}.
6616670d5cb033c8: A command open to a unit with the {a=0e}Resupply Module{/a} ability. It fully restores the EN and ammo of one adjacent unit, or one of the same squad (never the supplying unit itself).
fb4c1a05054514a9: A unit that is resupplied loses 10 Will{a=00}. That fall never takes Will below 100, and a pilot already under 100 loses nothing further.{/a}
1aa2139466c1522e: Resupply can normally be used only before moving, but a pilot with the {a=0e}Resupply Skill{/a} may use it after moving.
d2900207f3ac20e2: A squad holding a unit with a Resupply Module also gains the {a=0e}EN Regen{/a} squad bonus: right at the start of the player phase, {a=03}each unit recovers 10% of its EN for every Resupply Module unit in the squad{/a}.
fac3ff896590fa37: There are ways to restore HP and EN besides the Repair and Resupply Modules.
8b00641939957225: Many Spirits bear on restoring HP or EN. HP restoration in particular comes in many forms: yourself alone, one unit, a whole squad, or every ally. These are the main ones.
c4d60f7788d6e52b: Restores 30% of your own max HP.
375d131ac6a1e378: Restores 2500 HP to one chosen ally unit.
1721fd5696e57b18: Fully restores one chosen ally's EN and ammo.
5cd5d05bddf24f0f: Some Parts restore HP, EN or ammo. These are the main ones. A {a=0e}consumable Part{/a}, which vanishes once used, may also be used on another unit of the same squad. Battleships alone may use one on an adjacent squad.
6ef0eddb521dd778: At the start of your phase, restores 10% of max HP.
